breakdown_notes: This is Cengiz, Dube, Lindner & Zipperer, 'The Effect of Minimum Wages on Low-Wage Jobs', QJE 2019 (134(3):1405-1454). It is a difference-in-differences / bunching event-study using hourly-wage data from the 1979-2016 CPS across 138 state-level minimum-wage changes. The paper reports NO hardware, wall-clock time, GPU usage, or API cost -- standard for empirical economics. The replication is an author-provided Stata package driven by dofiles/master_QJE.do, using reghdfe for high-dimensional fixed-effects OLS regressions. It is CPU- and RAM-bound with NO GPU and NO external LLM API. The confirmed data footprint under codebase/data is 7.1 GB across 7,834 derived .dta files, several exceeding 1 GB (largest: totransfer.dta 3.3 GB, totransfer_ind.dta 2.1 GB, state_panels_with3quant1979_matched.dta 1.5 GB). The plan notes 'set matsize high; several derived .dta inputs are ~0.5-1.3 GB, so allow >=32 GB RAM.' Because all ~7,800 derived analysis .dta files ship with the package, the heavy raw-CPS build pipeline (master_QJE.do lines ~70-101) is skipped; the 9 headline steps each re-run reghdfe on these inputs to recompute Tables 1-4 and Figures 2-6. None of the 9 steps involve model training or inference in the ML sense, none repeat across seeds/configs (a single spec block per table), and none call any external API. Total runtime is dominated by loading multi-GB .dta files into Stata and running reghdfe with large fixed-effect sets -- well over the 5-minute 'light' threshold (plausibly tens of minutes to a few hours end-to-end), but far below 'heavy' since no GPU is required. Main non-compute prerequisite is a Stata license (Stata-MP/SE 15+) plus ado packages reghdfe, ftools, gtools, estout, moremata; Stata is not currently installed in the environment.
resource_type: CPU + RAM (Stata reghdfe); no GPU, no LLM API
commercial_license_required: Stata (per-seat license; annual/perpetual, hundreds to low-thousands USD depending on edition/tier)
parallelizable_notes: The 9 result do-files (Table1-4, Figure2-6) are independent and could run in separate Stata sessions concurrently, each first replaying master_QJE.do's global block and create_programs.do. Parallelism is bounded by available RAM (each session may hold 1-3 GB datasets).
estimated_wallclock_hint: tens of minutes to a few hours total on a single 32+ GB CPU machine
